thesis: Freedom’s history tests who is included in the declared community and who controls the standards of competence.

ideas.statement: Institutions can prevent capacities developing and then cite their absence to preserve control; formal equality alone does not repair inherited disadvantages.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Douglass offers individual testimony, not prevalence data; context explains without absolving, and limiting domination differs morally from losing protection against it.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Douglass offers individual testimony, not prevalence data; context explains without absolving, and limiting domination differs morally from losing protection against it.
